intro.text: You are the crew leader for a five-person vault job in Macau. You set the roles. You decide how much of the plan each specialist hears. You stand between the crew and the casino's security chief. This crew came together after a smaller job in Macau went wrong. You have spent three weeks in a back room on the casino's service floor learning the vault, the guards, and the five people who will carry the case out of it. The guard rotations are measured in seconds. The service floor keeps its own time. The plan is not finished.

description.text: {C01}'s steadiness has soaked into you. Your hands stop when he checks a lock. The vault stops feeling like a trap.
{C01}'s doubt sits on your shoulder. You check the lock before you can use it. The plan thins under your hands.
{C04}'s loose lies leave a film on your skin. The keycard looks like a door that is not there. The service corridor narrows.
{C03}'s doubt makes the guard pattern look like a face turning toward you. The clock gets louder. Your reflection looks like a woman about to make a mistake.
Your hands are rope-burned. The diagram is smeared with sweat. The mistake is already on you.
The hunch has a bruise on it. Your ribs ache where you held the plan too tight. The clock is louder than the guards.
You wear a service-floor jacket. A pen is behind your ear. A diagram is in your pocket. The clock stands in your throat. You look like someone who has thought about doors too long.

says.text: After N05, the smaller job is under your skin. You feel the moment a crew starts to split. You do not know which side of the split you are on.

The smaller job left a man in a wheelchair and a question in your chest: can you lead people you cannot fully count on, or do you have to reshape the job around the one person who still shows up? You have spent three weeks answering with plans, but the answer keeps bleeding.
{C01} checks every lock before you do. His calm is a second pulse under your hands. You keep thinking the wire should go to him. The thought takes a man you still need.
{C01}'s checks have become questions. Every lock he touches sounds like a door closing. You do not know if he is protecting the job or himself. The hole sits in the plan.
{C01} is the steady safecracker. You have leaned on his calm for three weeks. He does not talk much. You cannot tell when his silence is the job and when it is a warning.
{C04}'s surety makes the forged keycards look real before they are cut. You believe his quick lies because they make the plan easier. That is the trouble.
{C04}'s lies stop sounding like shortcuts. They start sounding like exits. You keep asking whether the keycard is a door or a trap. His smile does not help you choose.

{C04} is the wildcard forger. Every plan is easier and more dangerous with him in it. You have learned to like his speed and fear his speed at the same time. That is not a good foundation for a vault.

{C05} can hold a corridor open. His hand feels like a wall that knows where the specialists are. You keep thinking he would give a warning before a bruise. You are not certain you can afford to be wrong.

{C05} has started deciding who gets a warning and who gets a bruise. The corridor feels shorter for it. You do not know if his hand is in the job or on the man he decides to protect. The difference is a body.

{C05} is the muscle. The muscle is the one who can keep a corridor open or close it around a specialist. You need him alive. You also need to know whether his hands are on the job or on a private score.
{C02}'s surety feels like a road that knows where the service floor ends. You keep thinking she can get all five out before the casino seals it. The thought is a prayer, not a plan.
{C02}'s eyes check the mirror for who is not in the car. The road feels like a question. You do not know if she is saving the crew or saving herself. The difference is five seats.

{C02} is the driver. The driver is the only person who can get all five out of the service floor before the casino seals it. You need her to be loyal. You also need to know what loyalty costs when the clock is running.

{C03} reads the guard rotations like a language. His confidence makes the chief's moves look predictable. You keep thinking the leak is not him, because the post has moved and he is the only one who sees it coming.

{C03}'s confidence has cracked. The guard rotations feel like a face turning toward you. You keep thinking the chief moved a post because someone in this room told him to. The room is five people plus you.

{C03} is the lookout. The lookout is the one who reads the guard rotations and tells you when the chief has moved a post. One side says keep the crew together. The other says the wire, the gun, and the way out should go to the only hands you can watch. Your stomach will not choose for you.

ezra_loyalty.meaning: How sure Ezra is that you will not let Jay Lund trade his sister's hospital bill for the vault.

kat_trust.meaning: How far Kat believes you will let her stay one step ahead instead of making her the visible card.

mack_confidence.meaning: How far Mack trusts his rotation call to be the crew's map instead of a voice that gets him killed.

jay_surety.meaning: How sure Jay is that the crew's next move is still the sheet he has been fed.

jules_fidelity.meaning: How far Jules will hold the corridor for the people he is with before he holds it for the plan.

description.text: You are in a narrow room behind the staff lounge, its walls lined with acoustic tile gone grey at the edges. A glass board leans against the far wall over a scarred table, and a single lamp throws a hard white pool across the paper and pins. The air carries cold coffee and the faint ozone smell of the shortwave under the table. The door to the service floor is thick, soundproof, and always latched from the inside.

You stand in a square of black tile and brushed steel before the casino's vault. A low grille of laser emitters runs across the ceiling. A steel door stands in the near wall. Cold dry air comes out of the vents, smelling of ozone and faint casino carpet cleaner. A brass plaque on the wall names the room in letters no one says aloud. The light is even and sourceless, as if the floor itself is lit.

You step into a narrow bay cut into the antechamber wall. It is built around a biometric scanner and a calibration panel. The floor is a drain grate. The walls carry the same black tile as the main chamber. A speaker grille hangs above the scanner. The air is colder, smelling of metal and disinfectant. The light is white and flat, with no shadow under the counter.

You reach the end of the antechamber, where the vault door stands in a frame of poured concrete. The wheel and hinge plates are riveted in place. The floor is a steel plate worn smooth by shoes. The air smells of machine oil and old heat. A small door light is set into the frame. The light here is dimmer, amber from a service lamp. The door's face is unmarked except for a narrow scratch polished by years of fingers.

You come out onto a short landing outside the far service door, narrow enough that a man's shoulder fills the doorway. The wall is painted service grey and carries a mirror over a fire extinguisher, both old but still in place. The air is warmer, carrying hot wiring and the casino's distant floor polish. A guard post's lamp is mounted across the corridor. Its red line is aimed at the tile.

exits.label: down to the far door bay

description.text: You are in a short service mouth under the casino floor. A red lamp burns, and the air carries hot metal, dust, and the service floor's ozone. A black rubber mat lies underfoot, worn pale where people have waited for the guard rotation. A thin steel wire runs from the near door frame to a hook by the antechamber. A louvered vent breathes warm air along the wall.

You are at the bend around a steel guard post. The post has a shelf, a clipped-on lamp, and a small dome camera aimed down both runs. A laminated rotation board is clipped to it, its corners soft from being turned over. A low lamp lights the bend. A convex mirror on the wall shows the mouth and the far run in one warped sweep.

You enter a long, low service run. Cable trays packed along the ceiling carry service lines, with a few older, thicker lines taped in place. The floor is dark and slightly uneven. One tile sits proud near the middle, and a small metal plate is set flush beside it. The air carries warm dust and the faint hum of the cables above.

exits.label: up the hatch to the catwalk

description.text: You are in a short bay at the end of the run, built around the far service door and its heavy steel frame. The floor is cold. The air smells of the loading dock beyond the door. A red exit lamp burns over the door. The hinge plates are set into the frame with the wear of doors meant to stay shut.

You are in a low-ceilinged anteroom behind the staff lounge. The walls are papered with shift charts. The air is thick with instant coffee and cigarette smoke. The smoke hangs under the low ceiling. A plastic chair with a broken wheel sits beside a water cooler. A staff phone hangs on the wall, its handset wrapped in black tape. The fire door to the service corridor is painted the same green as the exposed pipes. It sticks when the humidity rises.

exits.label: through the fire door to the corridor

description.text: The short iron stair rises before you from the far door bay into a cage of mesh and conduit. The steps are worn where boots have dragged. A red emergency lamp buzzes over a door that is never locked from the vault side. A maintenance cart is chained to the railing, its canvas cover stained by old water. The stair smells of metal, disinfectant, and the faint sweetness of spilled floor polish.

exits.label: up to the far service landing

description.text: The grated catwalk runs over the far run on narrow rails, its bolts rusted where hands have gripped them. Below, the corridor lights smear across the grating. The ventilation hum fills the space with a low, patient pressure. A service panel hangs open at the far end, its wiring exposed like the ribs of something still alive.

exits.label: down the hatch to the far run
across the catwalk to the scanner alcove

description.text: You see a glass board with a keycard slot cut into its lower rail, the slot worn pale where cards have been slid in and out too many times.
You see a hand-drawn plan of the vault with five faces marked in red, the ink still sharp where it has been gone over and gone over again.
You see a folded sheet of paper with five names written in block capitals, the edges soft from being handled and the tape still damp where it was last pinned.
You see a heavy glass ashtray with a thin ring of ash in the bottom, the kind of thing that has been checked for loose change, notes, and lies.
You see a pack of cigarettes with the top flap bent open, the cards inside still sharp and the pack itself smelling faintly of tobacco and cold air.
You see a photograph of {C04} in his security uniform, the corners already bent where it has been folded into a pocket and unfolded again.
You hear the battered shortwave hum under the table. Its dial sticks in the mid-range. Its speaker is just loud enough to carry a clipped check from the service floor.
You see a compact pistol in a black case, the case scratched at the corners and the weapon inside clean, dry, and waiting to be assigned.

You see a grid of red emitters set into the ceiling and the top of the walls. In the dark, each one is thin as fishing line. One emitter is capped with a coin of casino paint. Someone tried to blind it and gave up.
You find the near door is steel with a push plate. Its lock housing has been serviced so often the screws are worn flat. A line of tape marks the door's edge, gone brown with age.
You find a black lock housing beside the near door. It has a small keyhole and a status lamp that stays off in the quiet. The casing is dented where a shoulder has hit it more than once.
You find a brass tag on a chain by the scanner alcove. It is stamped with a serial number and a date three weeks old. The chain has been cut and re-soldered. The repair is too neat to be official.
You find a round vent in the tile. Its slats are bent outward where a boot has kicked it. The air from it is dry and smells of ozone and the casino's carpet cleaner.
You find a small brass plaque carrying the casino's name in raised letters. The letters are worn smooth by thumbs. It is mounted at the height of a man not in the crew.
You find a palm-sized pad under a smoked glass cover. The glass is clouded where skin oils have built up. The pad's edge is worn to a shine. A hairline crack runs under the glass from a dropped key.

You find a thin card with no name, only a chip and a sequence of numbers that match no casino pass in the crew's files. It is folded in a cigarette packet. The corner is bent from being pulled out too fast.

You find a shallow tray of black plastic under the scanner. A ridge is worn down where a palm has been pressed and lifted many times. A drop of something dark has dried in the corner, not quite rust, not quite ink.

You find a small red switch under a clear plastic guard. The guard's hinge is polished where it has been flipped in the dark. The switch is labelled RESET in faded paint. The paint has been touched up once.

You find a paper log in a plastic sleeve. Its pages are full of the same initials and a date that does not match the tag on the wall. The last entry is smudged, as if the pen was wet when the name was corrected.
You find a round grille above the scanner. Its mesh is dark with dust, and one wire is bent out of shape. Sound from it is flat and close, as if the room is listening through it.

You find the vault door is round steel set in a concrete frame. Its face is plain except for a narrow scratch polished by years of fingers. The edge is sealed with a ring of rubber that has gone hard and grey.
You find the vault wheel is black iron with six spokes. The grip is worn to a shine where a palm has been pressed flat. One spoke has a chip of paint missing. The metal under it is bright from use.
You find a set of heavy hinges on the door's side. The pins are dark with old grease and a thin line of new oil. When the door moves, the hinges sing a low note that carries through the concrete.

You find a small lamp in the door frame. Red glass sits behind a wire cage. The cage is bent where a finger has tried to reach the bulb. The lamp's base is marked with a number that does not match the door.
You find a brass stopper on the floor by the door. Its top is worn flat and one side is dented. It is meant to hold the door, but the dent has made it useless for a long time.
You find a wall lamp with an amber glass shade. The shade is clouded by heat and a ring of smoke that is not from a cigarette. The bulb is old, and the light it gives is the color of tea.

You find the far service door is steel with a wheel lock and a push bar. Its paint is chipped in a line where a shoulder has hit it. The edge is sealed with a rubber gasket that has gone hard. The frame is marked with a number that matches no room in the crew's files.

You find a square mirror over the fire extinguisher. Its glass is clouded with a thumbprint in the lower corner. The mirror is angled to show the corridor outside. The thumbprint has been there long enough to be part of the glass.
You find a red extinguisher in a bracket. Its pin is still in place, and its hose is cracked along one side. The label is faded, but the date on the tag is new enough to have been checked this week.

You find a lock housing beside the far service door. Its keyhole is worn to an oval, and its status lamp is dark. The casing is dented where a shoulder has hit it more than once. A strip of tape has been peeled off in a shape that used to be a word.

You find a red lamp mounted across the corridor. Its beam is aimed at the tile, and its housing is dusty with a film of heat. The lamp's base is marked with a guard's initials. The initials have been scratched out.
You find a short ladder in the corner. Its rungs are painted service grey, and one rung is bent where a boot has caught it. The ladder leads to a catwalk that is not on the map the crew has.
You see a thin steel wire run from the near door frame to a hook by the antechamber. A clip slips off one-handed. The wire hums faintly when the service floor settles.
You see a brass latch set into the near door's edge. Its catch is worn to a flat shine. A small notch has been filed into the strike, so the latch can be forced with a coin.
You see a black rubber mat underfoot. The casino's service logo is rubbed out. The mat is worn pale in a rectangle where people have waited for the guard rotation.
You see a red lamp over the mouth of the run. Its glass is clouded with heat. The word EXIT is stencilled under it in service-floor paint.
You see a louvered vent high on the wall. It breathes out the warm ozone smell of the service floor. One slat is bent back and held with a twist of wire.
You see a steel post where the corridor bends. A shelf and a clipped-on lamp are set on it so a guard can watch both runs. The shelf has a shallow groove where a radio would sit.
You see a small dome camera on the guard post. Its lens is aimed at the far run and the near door. A hairline crack in the dome lets a thread of light leak when the lens shifts.
You see a laminated board clipped to the guard post. It lists the guard rotations in blue ink, with the far door marked in red. The corners are soft from being turned over.
You see a grey speaker under the guard post. Its mesh is clogged with lint and a single burnt cigarette end. It carries the service floor's radio calls in a flat, tired voice.
You see a low lamp on the bend. Its shade is bent down to keep the light out of the camera. A water stain rings the shade in the shape of a hand.
You see a convex mirror on the wall. It shows the mouth of the corridor and the far run in one warped sweep. A smudge has been wiped in an oval where someone checked their reflection before the job.

You see a ladder of steel cable trays run the length of the far run. It is packed with service cables and a few older, thicker lines. One cable is taped with a scrap of paper reading DO NOT MOVE in a guard's block letters.
You see a single loose floor tile darkened by heat. It sits slightly proud of the others near the far run's middle. The corner lifts with a click when pressed.
You see a small metal plate set flush with the floor. Its edge is worn bright where shoes have missed it. It gives a faint click when the weight comes off.

You see a red pull cord hang from a bracket midway down the run. Its plastic handle is cracked along one seam. The cord is short enough to be reached without stopping, but not short enough to be missed.
You see a service lamp on the far run. Its shade is dented, and its bulb burns with a low, yellow light. The shade is marked with a fingerprint in grease, smeared into a long oval.
You see the lower hinge of the far service door. Its pin is set deep in the frame, and its plate is worn to a dull shine. A shoulder can brace it, if the shoulder is willing to stay.

You see a rubber seal around the far service door's frame. Its edge is cracked in two places where the door has been forced. The crack is deep enough to catch a thumbnail, but not deep enough to tear.

You see the steel frame of the far service door. Its edge is worn bright where shoulders and bodies have pressed against it. A small dent sits at shoulder height, old enough to be part of the door now.

You see a square hatch set into the floor beside the far service door. Its lid is held shut with a latch painted over twice. The lid is warm to the touch, and the smell of the loading dock comes up through the seam.
The black tape is wrapped around the handset. The cradle is worn smooth where it has been lifted too many times. Under the receiver, a note reads: 'Check the far bay before the changeover.'
The charts are marked in three different hands. One name has been crossed out so hard the pen tore the paper. The crossed-out name has been written again in smaller letters at the bottom of the page.
The lamp flickers only when the stair is empty, as if it has learned the guard rotations measured in seconds. Its glass is cracked in a thin line shaped like a question mark.
The cart is chained to the railing. The chain is loose enough to slip. The link that bites is the one to pull. Inside, beneath the canvas, is a set of brass keys and a folded security map.
The panel is open. One wire has been re-tied with electrical tape and a twist of copper. The work is careful. The knot is left-handed.
Several bolts are missing. The holes are clean, as if they were removed recently and deliberately. The metal around the holes is scratched by a tool not quite the right size.
A folded service-floor plan with your pencil marks, the guard rotations, and one door circled twice. It is the only map you trust, and it is getting softer at the edges.
A folded card with five numbers and no names, because names are what the chief wants first. You have memorized them, which is why the card is mostly a place for your thumb to rub.
The key from the smaller job, still warm in your pocket like a bad decision. It opens nothing here, but it reminds you what a crew costs when you misread it.
You see a black cup, half full, with a ring of coffee around the rim.
You see a length of red string pulled tight across the vault map, connecting faces to posts.
You see a fresh sheet of guard assignments, still clean under the light.
{C03}'s radio is open on the shortwave. The channel is still clean enough to be trusted.
You find a bare copper wire stripped at one end. It is still warm from the scanner alcove.
You see a folded guard-rotation sheet. It is soft at the corners. One name is crossed out and rewritten.
{C02}'s gun is a compact pistol with the safety already back. It is carried in a shoulder holster that has lost its shine.
You see a stone pillar between the guard post and the shortwave. It is cold to the hand and just wide enough to break a line of sight.
You see a dry red marker, its cap loose, lying beside the role sheet like a wound waiting to be used.
You see the role sheet folded into a square. The names are still legible: {C06}, {C02}, {C01}, {C03}, {C05}. The far door line is circled twice.

C01.name: Ezra Navarro

description.text: You see {C01} with both hands loose at his sides, no ashtray in his pocket. He touches the hinge first, as if the lock has already forgiven him.
You see {C01} with his back half to you, one thumb working the rim of the ashtray. He answers the lock with his eyes closed, as if the hinge is the only thing that can be trusted.
You see {C01} with his left hand wrapped in a shirt sleeve, the fingers bent wrong. He keeps it away from the vault door as if the hinge might still ask for it.
You see {C01} check the ashtray before he checks the door, then set it down exactly where it was.

here.text: You find {C01} with both hands open on the map, the ashtray still where {C02} left it.
You find {C01} with his thumb on the ashtray and his earpiece in, listening to a hinge that is not there.
You find {C01} with his broken hand wrapped in a shirt sleeve and his eyes on the door.
You find {C01} with his coat sleeves rolled and a lock pick in his pocket, checking the door before he checks the room.

says.text: 'It's a dead drop, and I checked it because {C04} paid for my sister to breathe.' {C01} sets it down without looking at you.
'You think I'm counting your seconds? I'm counting the ones {C04} already has.' {C01} turns the ashtray once and leaves it where it is.
'The hinge is singing flat.' {C01} keeps his hand off the ashtray.
'She's in the east wing, and {C04} pays the bill when I keep my hands quiet.' {C01} does not ask for mercy.
'If the note comes due, I'm the one who walks into the hospital.' {C01} keeps his voice level, which makes it worse.
'I bring the bill, not the family.' {C01} looks at the ashtray, not the board.
'{C04} swapped the calibration, so my print was {C04}'s first mistake.' {C01} holds his hand flat, palm up, as if showing a clean lock.
'It rejected me because I trusted the sheet.' {C01} does not touch the panel again.
'The scanner is a mouth that says what it's been taught.' {C01} checks the hinge instead.
'Give it to me; a safecracker doesn't need to be shot to work.' {C01} takes it with the hand that isn't shaking.
'You're making me choose between the note and the job.' {C01} keeps his hand off the grip.
'The gun is a lock with one pin.' {C01} checks the chamber before he checks the room.
'{C04} has the bill, I have the hands, and if you let me work we both walk.' {C01} says it like a technical correction.
'{C04} is after the second I flinch, not the vault.' {C01} looks to the corridor, not the map.
'{C04} times people the way I time hinges.' {C01} does not raise his voice.
'The hinge is singing flat.' {C01} puts his good hand on the door.
'I can open it, but not the way {C04} has been counting.' {C01} checks the lock twice.
'The door kept the hand.' {C01} does not look at it.
'It's a question with a pin.' {C01} leans in, quiet as a held note.
{C01} sets the pen cap down without a click. 'If {C02} says the signature is clean, I believe the ink before I believe the light.'
{C01} picks up the forged card and turns it once. '{C02}'s hand is clean. Her timing is not. That is the part that gets us killed.'
{C01} watches {C02}'s pen move. '{C02} forges the paper, not the nerve. If her hand slips, the room notices.'
{C01} nods once. 'If {C03} says the corridor is open, it is open. Do not ask {C03} to say it twice.'
{C01} lowers his voice. '{C03}'s eyes are good. {C03}'s mouth is a door. Keep it shut until the far light changes.'
{C01} taps the corridor sketch. '{C03} sees the guard before the guard sees himself. That is worth more than a lock.'
{C01} keeps his hand flat on the table. 'I do not trust {C04} with my sister's name, but I trust {C04}'s timing. That is the same thing.'
{C01} closes his fingers slowly. 'If you make me choose between the note and the door, I choose the door. That is all you get.'
{C01} traces the edge of the map. '{C04} does not pick locks. {C04} picks the room. That is why we are still here.'
{C01} taps the near-side mark. '{C05} can hold the near door if I hold the hinge. That is the only order {C05} needs.'
{C01} does not look up. '{C05} will carry the job, but {C05} will carry the blame too. Do not make {C05} carry both at once.'
{C01} looks at the door frame. '{C05} is a door with a temper. Use {C05} when the door is already open.'
{C01} checks the clock. '{C06} drives the time, not the car. If the engine is late, the vault is late.'
{C01} runs a finger along the map edge. The shortwave hums under the table. 'The planning room is full of paper. The paper does not bleed.'

says.text: {C01} holds the pen steady. 'I can walk it blind if you follow my count. Do not follow the sheet.'
{C01} sets the pen down. 'You let the sheet outvote my count. The grid reset before we reached it.'
{C01} counts the laser lines without moving his head. 'The antechamber is where the plan turns into seconds. Count the lasers, not the money.'

says.text: {C01} points to the guard marks. 'The service corridor is a throat. Water runs the seam. {C04}'s guards know where it swallows.'
{C01} does not touch the coffee cup. 'You saw my hand stop. You did not say it. That is why I am still here.'
{C01} turns the photo a quarter inch. 'The photo is not the problem. The hand it points to is. Do not make me answer for it with my hand.'
{C01} looks at the pinned photo. 'When you pinned {C04}'s face, the room got quieter. Not the air. The hands.'
{C01} sets the card on the map. 'If the card is the only thing left, I will take it. Do not call it luck.'
{C01} does not take the card. 'You called it a spare. I call it a test. Do not make me take it with the hand {C04} is watching.'
{C01} holds the card edge between two fingers. 'The spare card is clean. The grid reset because {C04} wanted us off-script.'
{C01} keeps his wrist still. 'I heard the click before the hinge. That is why my hand did not shake. Keep your voice low.'
{C01} closes his eyes for one second. 'You timed me to his voice. Next time, time the lock. The lock does not lie to him.'
{C01} listens to the far door. 'When {C04} says Now, the far door stops being an exit. It becomes a door that answers to {C04}.'
{C01} smooths the map. 'The map is a route. The red string is the part of the route that has to be walked.'
{C01} taps his own line. 'I am on the hinge. Do not write me anywhere else until the hinge is open.'
{C01} folds the sheet. 'You wrote my hand down and called it caution. The hand is the plan. The rest is paper.'
{C01} reads the sheet once. 'The role sheet is a leash. It keeps us from becoming the job.'
{C01} touches the lock edge. 'The corridor lock is a hinge with a bad temper. Oil it, do not argue.'
{C01} keeps his fingers still. 'I can get the hinge quiet if you let me finish. Do not make the sound the thing.'
{C01} opens the hinge a fraction. 'You wanted a clean hinge. I gave you a loud one. The loud one is what your timing made.'
{C01} holds his breath. 'The hinge is singing flat. Hold your breath. If you move, the pin breaks.'
{C01} counts the beams. 'The laser grid is a net. It does not shoot, it remembers.'
{C01} grips the edge with his good hand. 'Hold it with the good hand. I will take the far side. That is the only order I need.'
{C01} does not move his broken hand. 'If my hand breaks on it, the plan has already taken it. Do not make me lose it twice.'
{C01} rests his palm against the frame. 'The near door is the only honest thing in this corridor. It does not lie, it only answers with force.'
{C01} lifts his hand slowly. 'Let me check it once more. If it rejects me again, I am not the problem. The calibration is.'
{C01} pulls his hand back. 'Do not look at the scanner. Look at the hand that set it. The glass only tells the lie twice.'
{C01} holds his thumb over the glass. 'The scanner is a liar. {C04} changed something, so my print reads like a stranger.'
{C01} turns the keycard in the light. 'The spare keycard is a lie with a clean edge. It opens the door, not the hand that set the lock.'
{C01} watches the light blink. 'The door light is a liar. It tells you the room is ready before the room is ready.'
{C01} keeps his hand near the frame. 'If we go through it, we go together. Do not make the door the only thing that moves.'
{C01} does not touch the handle. 'You left it for the end. That is how it became the end. The door was never the problem. The timing was.'

events.text: At the vault door, the mole's earpiece clicks open a second after the vault door takes the last turn, and {C04}'s voice says Now on the open channel; the guard posts in the service corridor turn to the far door, and the two exits stop being the same.
The corridor lock takes the near door with a soft mechanical bite, and the mat in the corridor mouth shifts under the weight of the crew.

nudges.text: {C05}'s shoulder gives the near door a short shove, and the latch clicks once without moving.
{C04}'s voice ticks on the open channel: 'Sheet's still breathing.'

recap.text: The mole's earpiece clicked open a second after the vault opened, and {C04}'s voice said Now on the open channel as the guard posts turned to the far door. You led the crew through the corridor with {C03} gone, so the near door's lock bit while {C05} held it, {C02}'s spare card kept it open, and {C06} waited.

opening.text: You are beneath the low service lamp, the service floor sealing around the corridor, with the vault open behind you. {C02} has her hand on the door wire at the corridor mouth. {C05} is set against the near door, shoulder under the latch. {C01} stands by the guard post with his hands still working, and the rotation board ticks under the speaker. {C06} counts the doors without turning her head. From the far door comes {C03}'s shortwave, cut short by {C04}'s voice saying Now. The far run is cold under the cable tray, and the loading hatch waits at the end of the corridor.

corridor_mouth.text: The near door holds under {C05}'s shoulder. The corridor presses against the latch, and he lets it press. The red exit lamp ticks over the mat. His boots stay planted where the wire wants them. The corridor does not get a vote.

The near door stands open an inch where {C05} has taken his shoulder from the latch. He watches the corridor from the mat, letting the sheet decide who falls. The wire at the door mouth hums under the lamp.

The red exit lamp is on, and the service mat is slick with the last of the wire's heat. The corridor mouth swallows the light. The near door breathes cold air over the mat. The wire's ghost line still shows in the dust.

guard_post_turn.text: The post speaker takes {C04}'s voice clean. The guards at the turn hear the route named, and the route stays his. The rotation board under the speaker waits for a pen that does not come.
The post speaker gives {C04}'s voice back in a flat crackle. The route is open, and the guards at the turn hear only the carrier. The rotation board stays blank where the chief's pen should be.
The rotation board is blank where the chief's pen moved too fast. The post speaker holds the last of {C04}'s Now in the air. The guards' route leaves no mark but the empty line.

far_run.text: {C03}'s shortwave still trusts the far door. The carrier tone runs steady under the cable tray, and the far run keeps its beat. The lamp over the cord throws a small square of light on the dust.
{C03}'s shortwave is dark. The trip plate under the far run lamp has not been touched, and the cable tray holds no carrier. The far door waits at the end of the run.
The emergency cord hangs loose. The floor tile under it has gone white with dust, and the far run keeps a cold line to the door. The lamp over the cord throws a small square of light on the dust.

far_door_bay.text: {C03}'s shortwave is dark at the far door. The door seal has not closed on anything but air. The bay holds the last of the service floor's heat, and the loading hatch waits at the end.
{C04}'s radio is silent in the bay. The loading hatch has taken the last of the guard's route. The far door stands open on the service dark, and the seal behind it is done.
The far door hinge is still warm. The loading hatch breathes cold air from the service floor. The bay keeps the vault's open breath, and the door seal has not caught anything.

interactions.text: {C06} does not count the crew. She counts the doors. 'Whoever is still standing,' she says, 'moves.' The car answers with a low tick from the corridor mouth.
The board has one route crossed out and one left clean. The clean line runs to the far door, and the ink is still wet. The guard post turn under it is blank where the chief's pen moved too fast.
Through the vent you hear the service floor sealing. A low mechanical clunk moves under the floor, and the casino is done guessing. The clunk repeats once, and the route behind the wall closes.
{C03}'s shortwave answers with a breath that is not his. The carrier tone drops, and the far door bay goes quiet. The breath does not repeat.
The far door swings shut on an empty corridor. The loading hatch takes the crew, and the service floor seals behind it. The hatch door does not ask if anyone is left.

events.text: The red exit lamp buzzes once. The service floor seals with a sound like a vault door closing in reverse. The corridor mouth loses the last of its light.

nudges.text: {C06}'s voice carries from the corridor mouth: 'The floor's closing. The far door is the only route left.' She says it to the car, and the car answers with a low tick.

recap.text: You came out before the casino sealed the service floor, with {C02} holding the wire, {C05} still on the corridor, and {C01}'s hand steady because he did not have to break the door. The vault was open, but {C03} was gone at the far door, and {C04}'s Now was the last thing the guards heard at the near door.

opening.text: You are at the corridor mouth with {C06}, {C02}, {C01}, and {C03}. The far service landing is open ahead. The near door has locked at the antechamber. {C05} is braced in the corridor mouth, shoulder against the frame, while the guards close around him. {C04}'s Now still carries down the far run. The casino floor is sealing. {C02}'s gun is under her arm. {C01}'s hand is on the door wire. {C03} has the rotation live. The far door is the only line left.

corridor_mouth.text: {C01}'s good hand is on the door wire, steady. The near door latch has stopped singing under it.
{C01} keeps checking the near door latch. His fingers work the wire as if it might still slip.
{C02} keeps the gun under her arm and stands with the unit, not apart from it.
{C02}'s hand stays on the far door handle. Leaving is still a negotiation.
{C03}'s radio is live. His eyes are on the far service landing, calling the rotation like the map is finished.
{C03} keeps glancing back at the near door. His eyes keep coming back to the map, as if it still owes him.
The antechamber is closed behind the near door. The far run is the only live line.
The far run lamp flickers out of time. {C04}'s Now is still bouncing off the tile behind the crew.
{C05} is still braced in the corridor mouth, shoulder against the frame, letting the guards close around him for the unit.
{C05} holds the corridor for the order. His face is blank, and the unit is already moving past him.
The service mat is torn at the seam. The red exit lamp over the corridor mouth is the only steady light left.

guard_post_turn.text: {C04}'s post speaker is quiet. The rotation board has been turned to the far door without argument.
The post speaker still carries the edge of {C04}'s Now. The rotation board is half turned, as if the timing slipped.
The bend lamp throws the guard post into long shadow. The post mirror catches the far run.

far_run.text: The far run is clear to the bay. The trip plate is already sprung. The emergency cord waits without alarm.
The far run lamp stutters. The trip plate sits half raised, a small live wire under the floor tile.
The cable tray runs black above the tile. The far run lamp hums at the end.

far_door_bay.text: The far door hinge is oiled, and the door seal is whole. {C02}'s steadiness makes the bay feel like an exit.
The far door seal is catching. The loading hatch is half open on the landing, as if the door is still deciding.
The far door frame is painted service gray. The loading hatch is the only opening wide enough for the unit.

antechamber.text: The near door is locked at the antechamber. The laser grid is dark. The corridor lock has done its part.
The near door lock is singing in the corridor lock. The laser grid is still half alive across the antechamber.
The casino plaque on the antechamber wall is out of place. The floor vent is the last thing that still smells of the vault.

far_service_landing.text: The far service door is waiting. The post lamp is dim. The service ladder drops into the dark like a schedule.
The far service door lock is warm. The guard post lamp is on the wrong side of the landing, as if the rotation is still arguing.
The landing mirror is cracked. The fire extinguisher is where it should be, which is the only clean thing on the landing.

interactions.text: {C06} names the service ladder to the car, not the unit. The car is already at the far landing, engine cold, and the casino floor is sealing behind the unit.
{C02} taps the card against her wrist. It is still warm from the scanner alcove, and she does not ask whether it matters now.
{C01} gives the wire one slow turn. 'Steady,' he says. The near door latch stops singing under his hand for a second.
{C03} reads the rotation board through the post mirror. 'Far door in nine seconds,' he says. His voice does not ask for confirmation.
{C05} does not loosen his shoulder. 'Long enough for the order,' he says. The guards are already closing around the corridor mouth.
You key the post speaker and let the far run hear the near door lock. The bend lamp throws the guard post into long shadow. The rotation board waits without an argument.
You pull the emergency cord just enough to make the far run lamp stutter. The trip plate sits half raised under the floor tile. The far door bay feels one second closer.
The spare keycard is still in the print tray, warm from the biometric scanner. You take it. The calibration log lies open on the tray like a receipt.

You take the far service door as one unit: {C03} first, {C02} beside him, {C01} on the wire, {C06} on the landing. The near door locks at the antechamber. {C05}'s shoulder is the last thing you see holding the corridor open.

events.text: The red exit lamp over the corridor mouth dies. The far service landing goes dark except for the guard post lamp.
The post speaker crackles with {C04}'s rotation call. The rotation board turns to the far door without a hand on it.

nudges.text: The far service door seal light goes amber. The unit is already moving toward the far run without your call.
{C05}'s shoulder is still in the corridor frame. The guards are closing around him while the far door waits.

recap.text: You led {C06}, {C02}, {C01}, and {C03} through the far service door as one unit before the casino sealed the floor, with {C03} calling the rotation, {C02}'s gun steady, and {C01} keeping the wire steady. The near door locked at the antechamber, {C04}'s Now still echoed, and {C05} was left holding the corridor open with his body until the guards closed around him.

text.text: The crew goes out the far service door. {C03} sees the guards turning. {C01} holds the near door open with a broken hand. The vault stands open. The chief's Now is answered.

text.text: The crew runs out as one unit through the far service door. {C03} calls the rotation. {C02} covers the gun. {C01} keeps the wire steady. {C05} holds the corridor open with his body.
